definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}, with operations inherited from Q. A unit of R means an element having a multiplicative inverse in R.
M_R is the R-span of M in V, namely all finite sums of r_j m_j with r_j∈R and m_j∈M. The canonical map R⊗_Z M→M_R sends r⊗m to rm; its injectivity is to be proved, not assumed.
For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex-linear map with E_ij(e_k)=δ_jk e_i for all k∈I, where δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise. This construction requires that e be a complex basis of V.

For natural a,r, binom(a,r) is the number of r-element subsets of {1,...,a}; in particular it is zero for r>a and binom(a,0)=1.

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0≤λ<p.

e=(e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v; for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Also y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. On the basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ, and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.

The map R⊗_Z M→M_R, a_R⊗m↦a_R m, is an R-linear isomorphism, M_R has an R-basis indexed by I, and its complex span is V. Each X_r and Y_r for r≥0 preserves M_R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λ X_λ)Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. More explicitly Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, and E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}.

inputs.statement: Let A and B be commutative semirings, S a multiplicative submonoid of A, and B an A-algebra which is a localization of A at S. Let T be an additive commutative monoid and A-module. Then the A-linear map f:T→B⊗_A T, f(t)=1⊗t, is a localized-module map at S: (i) multiplication by each s∈S on B⊗_A T is a unit in its semiring of A-linear endomorphisms; (ii) for every z∈B⊗_A T there exist t∈T and s∈S with sz=f(t); (iii) f(t₁)=f(t₂) implies that st₁=st₂ for some s∈S. A localization B at S means the images of S are units, every element has a numerator in A and denominator in S, and equality of images of two elements of A is killed by some element of S.

argument.text: For i∈I, E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i: its image is contained there by N002 and the coordinate formula, and it fixes every vector c e_i in that module. For i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j proves J_j⊆J_i; interchanging indices proves equality. Thus J_i=J_0=J. Every vector in M_R is the sum of its E_ii projections, and the independence of e in N001 makes this sum direct. Therefore M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. Each summand is generated by the projections of the finite basis in N002. Since e_i≠0, multiplication by e_i identifies J with this summand, so J is finitely generated. J cannot be zero: otherwise M_R=0 would contradict its complex span being V and the nonzero basis N001 with n>0 from H001.

produces.statement: J_i=J for all i∈I; J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C, and M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

argument.text: Define T=Q⊗_R J and μ:T→C by μ(q⊗c)=qc; balancing makes this a Q-linear map. Q is a localization of R at its nonzero elements: nonzero elements become units, every rational is a numerator/denominator with both in R (indeed integers suffice), and equality in Q is equality in the subring R, so the equality-killing condition holds with 1. M004 then says every z∈T satisfies sz=1⊗c for some c∈J and nonzero s∈R. Consequently μ(z)=c/s. If μ(z)=0, then c=0 in C, hence in J, so sz=0 and z=0 since s is invertible over Q. Thus μ is injective and its image is exactly the rational span of J. A finite R-generating list of J from F001 gives a finite Q-spanning list of T, because z=s^{-1}(1⊗c) and c is an R-combination of that list. Hence T is finite-dimensional.

produces.statement: T is finite-dimensional over Q and μ:T→C is injective with image span_Q J.

argument.text: Define r=finrank_Q T. Tensoring the direct decomposition F001 yields a Q-linear equivalence Q⊗_R M_R≃∏_{i∈I}T. Explicitly, on a pure tensor q₀⊗m, take its i-th coordinate to be q₀⊗c_i, where m=∑ c_i e_i with c_i∈J. The inverse takes a tuple whose entries are finite sums of q⊗c to the sum of the tensors q⊗(c e_i). Coordinate extraction is R-linear; these prescriptions are balanced and additive, and their composites fix pure tensors and tuples of pure tensors, hence all finite sums, so they are inverse. M001 applied to the I-indexed R-basis of M_R supplied by N002 gives an I-indexed Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; M002 gives its dimension n. M008 gives freeness of T over Q, while F002 gives finite generation. Thus M006 gives dimension of ∏_I T equal to ∑_I r=nr, and M005 applied to the displayed equivalence gives n=nr. Since n=λ+1>0 by H001, r=1.

produces.statement: finrank_Q T=1, with T finite-dimensional and μ injective.

argument.text: By F001 choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonzero generating list g_1,...,g_k of J, with k≥1. The vector 1⊗a in T is nonzero because its μ-image is a. Thus this singleton is Q-linearly independent (a scalar multiple equal to zero has scalar zero). F003 and M003 show that it spans T. For each 1≤j≤k, write 1⊗g_j as q_j(1⊗a) and apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. Since g_j≠0, q_j≠0. In particular all generators lie in the one-dimensional rational line Q a; this conclusion uses the rank computation, not merely the inclusion J⊂C.

produces.statement: There exists a family qcoefs of nonzero rational numbers indexed by {1,...,k} such that g_j=qcoefs_j a for every 1≤j≤k.

argument.text: Choose the family q from F004. Each nonzero rational q_j can be written p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a unit in R. To see existence without assuming a rank-one ideal theorem, write the rational as a ratio of two nonzero integers. For a positive integer d, divide off p repeatedly while it divides d. This terminates: p≥2 by H001, so each division of a positive divisible integer strictly decreases it; equivalently induction on d supplies a largest nonnegative exponent with remaining positive factor not divisible by p. Apply this to the absolute values of numerator and denominator; keep their signs in the remaining factors. Subtract the two exponents to get ν_j. The remaining ratio and its inverse both have denominators not divisible by p, hence belong to R, giving the unit u_j. Applying this finite construction to all indices gives the families in F005.

produces.statement: There exist integer exponents exps_j and units units_j∈R, for 1≤j≤k, with q_j=p^{exps_j}units_j.

argument.text: Choose νs and u from F005; let ν be their finite minimum and set b=p^ν a≠0. For every j, g_j=q_j a=p^{νs_j-ν}u_j b∈Rb, since νs_j-ν≥0. Conversely an index attaining the minimum gives g_j=u_j b, so b=u_j^{-1}g_j∈J. Thus J=Rb. This proves the required existential statement. F001 gives spanning of M_R by (b e_i), and N001 gives their R-independence: a relation divided by the nonzero complex scalar b is a relation on e. Hence they form an R-basis. The same proof applies to every nonzero scalar that generates J over R, since it uses only that scalar's nonzeroness and its generating property. F001, F002 and F003 provide the direct decomposition, injectivity of the tensor multiplication map, and dimension one.
